title: Dry‑run reconciler and gradual commit playbook for Optimize auto‑tuner
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Incident follow-up and operational playbook for the Optimize auto‑tuner. After the run on 2026-03-09 where aggressive batching/caching changes caused elevated tail latency for a subset of production requests, we need a robust dry‑run + staged‑commit reconciler that can validate recommendations against live traffic profiles without applying global changes immediately. This ticket captures the proposed reconciler design, runbook steps for operators, monitoring queries, and a set of mitigations (automatic rollback thresholds, safety fences, and visibility hooks) to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-03-09: Auto‑tuner deployed candidate batch/caching profile -> small fraction canary run -> 10:42 UTC spike in p95 for conversational workload
2026-03-09 11:05 UTC: Automated surge detector triggered rollback; incident declared
2026-03-10: Post‑incident triage - found recommendations ignored distribution skew (long prefix sessions) and dry‑run had incomplete KV cache modeling
2026-03-11: Design draft for dry‑run reconciler authored; added metric gating and hysteresis windows
2026-03-13: Implementation RFC merged; integration tests added for canary size and rollback hooks
2026-03-14: This ticket created to consolidate playbook, acceptance criteria, and action items
root_cause: The auto‑tuner optimizer generated batching/caching parameters optimized for median token sequences. The validation path (dry‑run) simulated average sequence lengths but did not adequately simulate long KV cache retention and prefix reuse. When applied to live traffic with heavy long‑prefix conversations, the new configuration increased token re‑computation and caused KV cache churn, increasing p95 latency. Additionally, the staged apply lacked a sufficiently conservative canary horizon and hysteresis, so a small canary produced noisy signals that flipped quickly into a global apply before stability could be assessed.
mitigation: Introduce a dry‑run reconciler that runs candidate configs against a shadow execution pipeline with realistic session reconstruction. Add explicit canary size and duration gates (canary-size: 0.5–2% of sessions; duration: min 30 minutes, preferred 2 hours for heavy tail workloads). Enforce hysteresis on metric gating (two consecutive windows of pass) and require KV cache hit-rate delta < 2% and p95 degradation <= 5% relative to baseline before global apply. Add automatic rollback triggers: p95 increase > 10% OR error-rate delta > 0.1% sustained for 5 minutes. Record decisions in an audit log and surface failure reasons in the Console rollout UI.
postmortem_summary: The incident was caused by a modeling gap between the optimizer's validation harness and production session characteristics. Rapid commit semantics amplified a transient noisy signal. No external customers reported data loss; customer impact: low but real latency regressions for a subset of conversational sessions. Immediate fix was to roll back the change and add temporary conservative defaults. Longer term: build the dry‑run reconciler, expand synthetic session generator, and codify playbook for staged commits. Ownership: Optimize infra + Serving runtime collaboration.
action_items: Liam Chen: Implement the dry-run reconciler service and integrate shadow KV cache module
Sofia Martinez: Expand synthetic session generator to include skewed long-prefix conversations (param sets: short/median/long)
Dev: Add metric gating with hysteresis and canary duration enforcement in rollout controller
Ops: Create durable audit log entries for each candidate apply and expose failure reasons in Console
QA: Add end-to-end tests that simulate KV cache churn and validate rollback triggers
PM: Update runbook and customer communication templates for latency regressions
acceptance_criteria: Dry‑run reconciler executes candidate configs against shadow execution with a realistic session workload and returns pass/fail with a detailed delta report
Rollout controller enforces canary-size and canary-duration gates and requires two consecutive passing windows before global apply
Automatic rollback triggers are implemented and tested (p95 > 10% OR error-rate delta > 0.1% for 5 minutes)
Console shows audit trail entries for each apply with links to raw dry‑run reports and the observed metric deltas
E2E tests for long‑prefix session scenarios are green in CI
notes: Trade-offs discussed: more conservative canary reduces optimizer throughput gains; added complexity in reconciler increases maintenance surface. Decision: prioritize reliability for next two quarters while collecting richer traffic profiles to eventually relax canary gates. Consider feature flag to allow advanced customers to opt into aggressive profiles behind SLAs. Follow-on ticket will evaluate ML‑guided anomaly filters to suppress noisy canary signals.
